data.exact_reserve_text: During 2016, net ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2014 & prior) reduced by GBP 6.7m. This was mainly due to favourable claims development over the year in the Director's & Officers, Marine Liability and Aerospace classes. The Airline Liability class also benefited from a GBP 2.7m takedown in the large 2008 Air France loss. These reductions were offset by net ultimate claims increases in the A&H and General Liability classes, partly due to increased exposure estimates as inwards premium from binders were revised upwards.

data.standardized_narrative: Using the gross claims development triangle, gross claims for prior underwriting years (2014 and earlier) reduced by approximately GBP 11.95m (about 2.90% of opening gross reserves). The movement reflects favourable development in Directors & Officers, Marine Liability and Aerospace (including a takedown on the large 2008 Air France loss), which was partly offset by adverse movements in Accident & Health and General Liability driven by increased exposure estimates from binders. The report states a net (after reinsurance) prior-year release of GBP 6.7m; the gross movement has been calculated from the published gross claims development triangle.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development gross movement was not stated explicitly as a gross figure; the report states a net prior-year release of GBP 6.7m (after reinsurance). A gross PYD was calculated from the published gross claims development triangle (pages 37-38) for underwriting years 2011-2014, yielding a gross release of approximately GBP 11.95m. Event-level amounts quoted in the narrative (eg. GBP 2.7m takedown on the Air France 2008 loss) appear to be net figures in the narrative and have been treated with lower confidence. No RITC was identified that would distort the triangle.
